newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks close higher, rebound from losses.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks close higher, rebound from losses.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks ended higher on Friday, clawing back some of Thursday's heavy losses as investors continued to see more upside in prices in the medium term, brokers said.
The Hang Seng index rose 83.17 points to 13,393.93 after falling 220.19 points on Thursday. Over the week, the index gained 277.14 points, or 2.11 percent.
"You just can't keep a good market down these days," said James Osborn, sales director at ING Barings. "Basically we were sold down heavily yesterday and it is just a rebound really."
Turnover was HK$7.46 billion, sharply lower than Thursday's HK$13.58 billion.
"It is linked to the stock exchange investigation," said Frederick Tsang, head of research at PrimeEast Securities.
The Stock Exchange of Hong Kong is looking into opening transactions on Thursday when the Hang Seng shot up 213 points to an all-time high of 13,744.30, then shed all of its gains.
"I think it is really a bit cautious," added Tsang. Some investors had decided to stick to the sidelines this session after Thursday's gyrations and ahead of the weekend, analysts said.

"Most investors are actually sidelined to wait to see whether the Dow can rise futher," said Tony Yung, research director at Tai Fook Securities. "I think that the market should consolidate...I think Hong Kong now is not especially cheap."
But Osborn said the general consensus in the market was that the Hang Seng offered valued above 13,000 points.
"The Hong Kong market is not expensive. There is a real feel good factor in Hong Kong - property prices are up, retail sales are supposed to be recovering," he said.
Osborn said retail activity had also picked up in the market.

Citybus Group Ltd ended its first trading day on the exchange with solid gains. Shares in the bus operator opened at HK$1.43 per share compared with an issue price of HK$1.42 and closed the day at HK$1.55.
Pearl Oriental shares were among the most active of the session and fell HK$0.25 to HK$4.625.
Property shares were generally weak on Friday. Sun Hung Kai Properties fell HK$1.00 to HK$96.00 and Henderson Land closed HK$0.50 lower at HK$77.75. Cheung Kong shed HK$0.50 to HK$68.00.
HSBC Holdings ended unchanged at HK$161.00 but Hang Seng Bank rose HK$1.25 to HK$93.25.
